meta.title: Operation of Mechanical Grinder in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To rapidly reduce the particle size of dried crude drugs and plant materials using high-speed mechanical grinding blades for preparation of uniform powders for extraction and standardization.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for size reduction of moderately hard dried plant materials including leaves, flowers, stems, seeds, and barks prior to extraction or powder characterization.
procedure: Ensure the crude drug material is thoroughly dried before grinding — moisture content above 8% causes clogging and uneven grinding.
Break large pieces of dried plant material into smaller fragments (< 3 cm) manually before loading.
Remove the grinding bowl from the grinder and confirm it is clean and dry.
Place the dried drug material into the grinding bowl — fill to not more than 1/3 capacity.
Secure the lid firmly on the grinding bowl — check the lock mechanism.
Place the bowl assembly in the grinder unit and lock into place.
Switch on the grinder using short pulses (2–3 second bursts) initially to break the material, then continuous run for fine grinding.
After 30–60 seconds of grinding, switch off and allow the blades to stop completely.
Unclip and open the bowl carefully — avoid inhaling the fine dust cloud released.
Check the particle size by passing through the target sieve; return coarse fraction for further grinding.
Repeat grinding-sieving cycles until the desired powder grade is achieved.
Collect the final powder in a labelled airtight container.
Clean the grinding bowl with a dry brush, then rinse with the extraction solvent to be used; finally wash with water and dry completely.
Record: drug name, initial and final weights, sieve size used, and grinding time in the logbook.
precautions: Wear a dust mask (N95), safety goggles, and gloves during operation.
Never open the grinding bowl while the blades are still moving — wait for complete stop.
Do not grind wet or fresh plant material — moisture corrodes the blade and causes jamming.
Do not grind resinous materials for extended periods — resin heats up, melts, and coats the blades.
Clean thoroughly between different drug materials to prevent cross-contamination.
Do not exceed the rated capacity of the grinder — overloading stresses the motor.
Inspect blades before each use — dull or nicked blades give non-uniform particle sizes.
Ground the grinder to prevent static charge accumulation when processing fine, dry powders.
